nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces. If every $f_k$ is differentiable on all of $\mathbb{R}^{d_k}$, then for every input $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the layer $f_j$ is differentiable at the forward pass of $x$ through the first $j$ layers for every $j < n$.
nodes.title: Differentiable layers are differentiable along every forward pass

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, let $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $a_j \in \mathbb{R}^{d_j}$ for the forward pass of $x$ through the first $j$ layers. The network is differentiable along the forward pass of $x$ through its first $n$ layers when $f_j$ is differentiable at $a_j$ for every $j < n$.

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, let $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $N_j : \mathbb{R}^{d_0} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_j}$ for the forward pass through the first $j$ layers. If $f_j$ is differentiable at $N_j(x)$ for every $j < n$, then $N_n$ is differentiable at $x$.

nodes.summary: For a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, the forward pass through the first $n$ layers is the map $N_n : \mathbb{R}^{d_0} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_n}$ given by $N_0(x) = x$ and $N_{n+1}(x) = f_n(N_n(x))$, that is, $N_n = f_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_0$.

nodes.title: The network at fixed parameters

nodes.summary: Given layer widths $d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a feedforward network with widths $d$ is a sequence of arbitrary maps $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d(k)} \to \mathbb{R}^{d(k+1)}$, one for each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, where $f_k$ is the map computed by layer $k$ and $\mathbb{R}^n$ carries its Euclidean structure.
nodes.title: Feedforward network

nodes.summary: Given layer widths $d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and parameter dimensions $p : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a parametrized network is a sequence of arbitrary maps $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{p(k)} \times \mathbb{R}^{d(k)} \to \mathbb{R}^{d(k+1)}$, one for each $k \in \mathbb{N}$: layer $k$ sends parameters $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{p(k)}$ and an input $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d(k)}$ to $f_k(\theta, x)$.
nodes.title: Parametrized feedforward network

nodes.summary: For a feedforward network $N$ with layer widths $d$ and a natural number $j$, the shifted network has layer widths $i \mapsto d(j + i)$, and its layer $i$ is layer $j + i$ of $N$. It is made of the layers of $N$ from layer $j$ on.
nodes.title: Shifted network

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
